sector.name: Wires & Cables
sector.description: Cable makers riding power, infra and export demand

sectorSummary.overview: Demand remains supportive, but strong reported growth masks more modest physical volume growth and uneven execution. Polycab and KEI retained their outlooks, APAR and Dynamic face export or commissioning uncertainty, and RR Kabel lowered its FY27 volume target.

trends.text: Metal-linked realizations lifted reported growth faster than physical volumes: APAR conductor volumes fell, Dynamic grew Q2 volumes about 6%, and Polycab and RR Kabel reported single-digit W&C volume growth.
Managements continue to see demand from power infrastructure, renewables, housing and industrial investment, supporting their growth plans.

tailwinds.text: Transmission, distribution and renewable-energy investment remain important sources of cable and conductor demand.
Distribution reach and stronger customer access support growth: KEI reported a 59% distribution sales mix, Polycab saw channels outgrow institutions, and RR Kabel is deepening market penetration.

headwinds.text: Geopolitics and shipping disruption constrain export execution: APAR has DDP goods in transit, Dynamic cites freight and insurance costs, KEI has slightly lower H1 exports, and Polycab reports booking and shipping delays.
Higher raw-material values increase working-capital demands or change ordering behaviour, making cash discipline important alongside revenue growth.

opportunities.text: APAR has about ₹1,000 Cr of cable orders linked to Google and Amazon data centres; Dynamic is still developing its offering, with customer testing to follow product readiness.
KEI targets Sanand Phase 2 commercial production by March 2027, while Polycab expects its EHV plant to commission in FY28, expanding higher-voltage capability on different timelines.

risks.text: RR Kabel lowered FY27 W&C volume guidance to 14-15% from 16-18%; its FMEG business returned to a Q2 loss while retaining the full-year breakeven goal.
APAR warned that elevated oil margins include gains and are not normal margins, limiting how far current group profitability can be extrapolated.
Polycab awaits the NCLAT order in the stayed Asier Metals matter; its assessment of no material impact remained management’s view as of the call.

insights.text: FMEG outcomes diverged: Polycab grew 124% with a 10.1% EBIT margin, while RR Kabel grew 42% but reported a roughly ₹12 Cr segment loss.
Margin targets remain period- and basis-specific: KEI expects roughly 11% FY27 EBITDA margin, Polycab retains an 11-13% medium-term W&C EBITDA range, and RR Kabel targets 9.5% W&C EBIT in FY27.

Polycab India Ltd.whatChanged: W&C revenue growth accelerated to 47%, with domestic W&C up 50%; exports rebounded 85% sequentially, while management left its Project Spring outlook unchanged.
risks: The Asier Metals CIRP admission was stayed, with the NCLAT order still awaited as of the call; management expected no material business or financial impact.
International shipping delays and geopolitical uncertainty continued to affect export bookings, despite Q2 export growth of 17% YoY and 85% QoQ.
Favourable product/channel mix and operating leverage supported quarterly margins; management warned that mix and seasonality can cause margins to normalize.
highlights: W&C Q2 volume growth was mid-to-high single digit on a strong prior-year base; wires grew in early double digits and cables in mid-single digits.
FMEG grew 124% YoY, recorded 10.1% EBIT margin and delivered its seventh consecutive profitable quarter.
Average working-capital cycle was about 11 days in Q2 due partly to higher payable days from raw-material letters of credit; management expects normalization toward 45-50 days.
The EHV plant is expected to commission in FY28; management cited possible April or May commissioning.

R R Kabel Ltd.whatChanged: Management lowered FY27 W&C volume guidance to 14-15% from the earlier 16-18% range despite strong revenue growth; FMEG reported a Q2 loss after Q1 breakeven while retaining its full-year breakeven goal.
risks: FY27 W&C volume guidance was lowered to 14-15% from 16-18% amid near-term volatility; management did not offer a focused FY28 volume forecast.
FMEG posted an approximately ₹12 Cr Q2 segment loss; the full-year breakeven goal depends on the stronger H2 season.
Higher raw-material prices are increasing finance/working-capital needs, and debt may rise; the ₹200 Cr Rajasthan land acquisition is additional to FY27 capex.
highlights: Q2 W&C volume growth was high single digit, with wires growing in double digits and cables in single digits; exports grew faster than domestic.
Management said exports were about 32% of Q2 sales and expected a 30%-35% share in H2; exact export revenue was not disclosed.
The proposed UM Cables transaction is for approximately ₹77 Cr, subject to closing conditions; management said not to assume a material FY27 revenue contribution before gaining control.
